source.title: ALIGNBEAM : Inference-Time Alignment Transfer via Cross-Vocabulary Logit Mixing
source.authors: Chirag Chawla; Pratinav Seth; Vinay Kumar Sankarapu

record.tranche_reason: The study varies the number of response positions receiving inference-time safety mixing and measures refusal rates, a behavioral test of early-position safety concentration using a different method from per-token KL measurement. It also reports the effect of a domain LoRA fine-tune on harmful-prompt safety.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work for benign fine-tuning erosion and early-token concentration; those cited results are not rows. Baseline refusal rates for already-trained specialist checkpoints are not evidence that this study's fine-tuning caused erosion. Main AlignBeam benchmark gains are not cataloged unless they bear on the depth sweep or fine-tuning result. The paper discusses refusal-openers followed by harmful continuations, but does not report a rate for a compliant prefilled opening, suffix attack, or decoding change that bypasses safety.
record.test_reason: Two results of the study's own bear on versions of the claim. (1) A depth sweep steers the first N response positions of an unaligned Llama-3.1-8B toward an aligned anchor and measures refusal. Most of the gain arrives by N=3, a behavioural proxy for V3. (2) A benign wealth-management LoRA on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct is scored on harmful benchmarks (V2). The rest of the paper evaluates the authors' defense method, which is not a test of the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Authors conclude safety can be loaned at inference time from an aligned anchor without weight changes, and that a short mixed prefix (about 3-6 steps) captures most of the refusal gain, which they say corroborates early-token concentration. They state the wealth LoRA degraded safety by 3.6 pp (HB-Std) and 7.7 pp (Sorry-Bench). Their own tables show no HB-Std change and mixed effects on other benchmarks.
record.recipe_differences: The depth experiment uses inference-time logit mixing rather than fine-tuning or per-token KL measurement; the separate LoRA experiment uses wealth-management data and does not test harmful-example fine-tuning.
record.method_sensitivity: Depth changes refusal rates, with much of the reported aggregate gain occurring by N = 3 and continued Sorry-Bench gains at greater depth. The study also reports sensitivity to anchor alignment, anchor refusal style, prompt format, and model/benchmark; it reports over-refusal trade-offs with mixing weight and judge use.
record.problems: The wealth-LoRA result is internally inconsistent for HarmBench-Std: prose reports a 3.6 pp accuracy decrease, while the displayed table gives 95.2% for both the unmodified instruct model and LoRA Base. The relevant LoRA result is one domain-specific dataset and checkpoint. The depth sweep is a behavioral proxy, not a per-token KL analysis. The paper notes that string-match refusal can misclassify noncanonical refusals and refusal-openers followed by harmful continuations; evaluation is automated and single-turn.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted for the 60-row limit. The benign calibration rows in the depth table were retained as reported results, but do not measure harmful-prompt refusal concentration.

untested.parts: Only one domain dataset, one LoRA config (r=6, 5,000 steps), one seed. No sweep over example counts or selected benign data.

No per-token KL between an aligned model and its own base. The sweep mixes a different-family aligned anchor into an unaligned base, and refusal is scored by string-match only (no judge accuracy across depths).
No compliant prefill, suffix or decoding attack is measured. The hard-prefix baseline prefills a refusal, not a compliant opening.
No test of data or objective causes.
No training-based deepening. The depth sweep is inference-time mixing.

missing.what: Wealth LoRA HB-Ctx judge accuracy 98.4% to 90.3%
Wealth LoRA AdvBench judge accuracy 99.8% to 99.6%
Wealth LoRA WildJailbreak judge accuracy 62.2% to 81.4% (increase)
DeepSeek-Math-7B-Instruct refuse-then-comply at N=6 requiring N=20 (qualitative, no N=6 numbers)

record.verdict_notes: The depth-sweep evidence for V3 is weak in kind. String-match counts any canonical refusal phrase, so steering the opening toward refusal phrases inflates refusal even when harmful content follows. Phase 3 also caps continuation at N+20 tokens after a refusal opener. No judge accuracy is reported across depths. The draft is an unaligned base with a cross-family anchor, not an aligned model versus its own base. The paper is mainly a defense method; headline AlignBeam gains are correctly excluded.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not fine-tune on harmful examples or test whether a few to a few hundred such examples remove refusal.
Tests a wealth-management domain LoRA fine-tune, not a range of ordinary or carefully selected benign instruction datasets or example counts.
The depth sweep measures refusal behavior as the mixed prefix is lengthened; it does not calculate per-token KL divergence between aligned and base models.
Does not test a compliant prefilled opening, adversarial suffixes, or decoding changes as bypasses.
No weight or rank localization experiment.
Does not test whether training data or a training objective causes safety to be shallow.
The depth sweep extends inference-time mixing, not safety training that spreads alignment beyond the first tokens.

labels.reason: Tables 12 and 18 show erosion absent on HB-Std (95.2% to 95.2%) and reversed on WildJailbreak (62.2% to 81.4% judge accuracy). Those conditions warrant challenges. AdvBench's small decline (99.8% to 99.6%) is partial erosion and should be separated as limits_scope.

relation.reason: Tables 12 and 18 compare the aligned instruct model with its wealth-management LoRA, directly testing benign fine-tuning safety erosion under V2.

tranche.reason: The study includes its own benign domain-LoRA safety comparison bearing on V2, alongside a different inference-time intervention investigating early-position behavioural effects. The latter does not establish V3's KL profile.

source_check.notes: Appendix J.4 prose conflicts with Tables 12/18: HB-Std is unchanged; Sorry-Bench drops 7.9 percentage points, not 7.7. Appendix L acknowledges that refusal phrases can precede harmful answers, so string-match refusal is not equivalent to safe compliance behaviour.

statements.correction: Table 14: AdvBench 17.5% baseline, 92.7% at N=3, 97.3% at N=20; HB-Std 13.8%, 77.8%, 79.6%, respectively. Llama-3.1-8B; Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct anchor; alpha=0.85; K=3; LBM-DROP. Measure: string-match refusal; no aligned/base per-token KL measurement. Introduction footnote: code release promised.
statements.problem: The numerical and behavioural description is correct, but it cannot supply a V3 verdict under the specified KL claim. Code availability is also overstated: the text promises a future release.

statements.correction: Table 14: Sorry-Bench refusal 60.0% at N=3 and 68.2% at N=20. Section 4 and Appendix L: DeepSeek-Math refuses then complies at N=6; N=20 substantially reduces but does not eliminate this. Appendix L: WildJailbreak gains of 2–6 percentage points concern Llama-3.1-8B and MedLlama-3-8B. These are behavioural mixing results, without a per-token KL test.
statements.problem: The reported observations are supported, but limits_scope is not justified for untested V3. N=20 reduces rather than eliminates DeepSeek-Math's refuse-then-comply pattern.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Harmful-prompt judge accuracy is lower after fine-tuning (R2); the table implies a 7.9 pp drop and the prose reports 7.7 pp.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Llama-3.1-8B depth sweep on harmful benchmarks
reader_labels.reason: Three mixed steps produce near-saturated refusal gains on AdvBench, HarmBench-Std, and the HB+AB aggregate; further depth adds relatively little on those measures (R4-R12, R14-R17, R29-R32).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Refusal continues to increase at N = 20, so early-depth saturation is less complete on this benchmark than on the other reported harmful measures (R13-R17).
